answer: The echo multiplier is published, charged in relic, and yarrow lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 8 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 989 identities would post 4949 proofs and burn roughly 2 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
